settings.heading: I’ve tried probiotics already. What makes this different?
settings.content: Probiotics put more bacteria into your gut. Our formula targets the system that’s meant to sweep bacteria out to begin with. When that system isn’t working, adding more bacteria won’t fix it. It only adds fuel to the problem.

settings.heading: Rifaximin didn’t work for me. Why would this?
settings.content: Rifaximin wipes out the bacteria, but it doesn’t address why they came back. Your gut’s cleaning wave stays switched off, so the bacteria grow back, which is exactly why so many people relapse within a few months. Our formula goes after the root cause that Rifaximin leaves untouched.

settings.heading: My biggest problem is urgency, rushing to the bathroom after I eat. Can this help?
settings.content: It’s the number-one reason people come to us. That urgency happens when bacteria in your small intestine ferment your food before your body has a chance to absorb it. As the bacterial buildup clears, fermentation calms down, and the urgency fades with it.

settings.heading: Do I take this forever, or is it a 90-day protocol?
settings.content: That depends on what slowed your gut down in the first place. If the trigger is ongoing, like a medication, an underactive thyroid or chronic stress, plan on taking it daily long-term. If it was a one-off event like an infection or a round of antibiotics, 90 days is usually enough for a full reset.

settings.heading: Why drops and not capsules?
settings.content: A capsule has to make it through your stomach and dissolve before anything gets absorbed. Liquid drops absorb right through your mouth, so they get to work sooner. Drops are also the natural way to take oil-based botanicals like oregano and clove. They’re oils, and a dropper delivers them the way they’re meant to be taken.

settings.heading: What stops this from coming back like everything else I’ve tried?
settings.content:
Everything you’ve tried so far, Rifaximin included, only targeted the bacteria. None of it fixed the reason the bacteria built up in the first place.

Bacteria pile up in your small intestine when your gut’s built-in clearing system, the Migrating Motor Complex (MMC), stops doing its job. Antibiotics and herbal protocols can bring the numbers down, but if the MMC is still offline, the bacteria rebuild, often within weeks.

Our formula addresses both.

settings.heading: Why Your Gut Never Fully Resets
settings.body:
Your small intestine comes with its own cleaning system: a wave of contractions that sweeps bacteria out between meals. Stress, medications and diet can switch it off. Bacteria start to pile up, and the longer they stay, the thicker the protective shield they build around themselves. That shield is called biofilm, and it keeps them from being cleared out.

It’s a cycle that doesn’t stop on its own.

settings.body: Clove breaks down the shield bacteria hide behind. Oregano clears out what’s left exposed. Ginger restarts your gut’s cleaning wave so bacteria can’t move back in.* Sequenced. Targeted. Unlike anything you’ve tried before.
